topic: Why course completion rates depend on who is counted
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Why course completion rates depend on who is counted
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. An imaginary training provider compared two online courses. In the first, seventy of one hundred registered learners submitted the final project. In the second, sixty of sixty-five learners who opened the first lesson submitted it. The provider advertised the second course as having a higher completion rate. A reviewer asked why the two denominators had been defined differently.

B. Registration and starting a lesson were not equivalent events. Some registered learners might never open a course, perhaps because they changed plans or could not access the platform. If the first course excluded non-starters, its completion rate would change. The available figures did not say how many people had opened its first lesson, so a fair comparison could not yet be calculated.

C. The final project also differed. The first course required an independently designed investigation; the second required a short reflection on provided examples. Submitting these tasks might involve different amounts of work. A high submission rate did not necessarily indicate stronger learning, nor did a demanding task automatically make a course better. The reviewer wanted a common assessment of what learners could do afterwards.

D. Staff suggested a voluntary follow-up exercise six weeks after completion. This could reveal delayed retention among those who participated. It could not, by itself, describe everyone who registered. People willing to return might be more confident or have more free time. The report would need to show how many were invited and how many responded, together with the original entry requirements.

E. The provider revised its dashboard to show registered learners, starters and submitters separately. It also described the final task and removed the simple ranking. Prospective learners could then consider the evidence alongside practical needs such as access and workload. The revised dashboard did not solve every comparison problem. It made the definitions visible, which allowed a reader to recognise which conclusions the numbers supported and which remained uncertain.

questions.prompt: How many registered learners were counted for the first course?
questions.explanation: 依据原文“one hundred registered learners”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。 数量允许本题列出的等值数字写法；单位接受明确列出的英美拼写。

questions.prompt: What is the central problem with the advertised comparison?
options: The second course had no final project.
Every registered learner had submitted work.
Both courses counted precisely the same event.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“the two denominators had been defined differently.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: the two denominators had been defined differently.

questions.prompt: What missing figure prevents recalculating a comparable rate?
options: The first course’s number of registered learners.
The date of the second course’s reflection task.
The number who opened the first course’s initial lesson.
The second course’s number of submitters.
answers: The number who opened the first course’s initial lesson.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“did not say how many people had opened its first lesson”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.explanation: 依据原文“delayed retention”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: Why might follow-up volunteers not represent all registrants?
options: They were required to join before registration.
They had all failed both original projects.
Their entry requirements had been removed.
They could have greater confidence or available time.
answers: They could have greater confidence or available time.
